title: wwfl-world-heavyweight
label: "Stone Cold" Mcdowd

won.source: Defeats the reigning champion by pinfall (a reversed finisher) on the fed's own served 11 January 1998 broadcast.

lost.source: Submits to a challenger's finishing hold at the fed's own annual flagship event, with a returning wrestler serving as special guest referee.

note: The wrestler this holder defeated to open this reign is recorded only by billing on the fed's own 11 January 1998 broadcast; not minted as a character.

won.source: Defeats the reigning champion by submission at the fed's own annual flagship event.

lost.source: Loses by pinfall (Doggpounder) to Dogg at the fed's own Memorial Mayhem pay-per-view; the special guest referee, the WWFL president, is revealed to have been working with the challenger throughout the match.

won.source: The fed's own 11 March 1998 broadcast: Kory Shinlever is ambushed backstage before reaching the ring and never arrives; the referee awards Steel Machine the win and the vacant belt on a no-show.

lost.source: Per the same 27 May 1998 broadcast recap, lost the belt to the challenger below.

won.source: Took the belt from the previous holder at the fed's own annual flagship event, outside a formal title match; first served as champion at the Spring Breakout '98 pay-per-view.
Not attested to a date in the held record.

lost.source: Stripped on air by the WWFL president for disrespecting the belt.

title: wwfl-cage
label: The Ultimate Giant

won.source: Per the fed's own 27 May 1998 broadcast recap of the sequence of champions.

lost.source: The fed's own annual flagship broadcast records the belt changing hands outside a title match, in a post-match assault.

note: The record does not state a formal fall or submission ending this reign.

title: wwfl-intercontinental
label: Darren Patrick

won.source: Per the fed's own 19 February 1998 broadcast, recalling this title change.

lost.source: The same broadcast recalls this reign lasting only a week; the record does not say who ended it or how.

note: The record does not say who ended this reign or how.

title: wwfl-intercontinental
label: The Trickster

won.source: The fed's own 27 May 1998 broadcast states this champion had held the belt for almost five months by that night, calling it the longest reign in the promotion's own history.

note: Retains through the held record's last-served Intercontinental Championship match, 27 May 1998, which ends without a clean decision.

won.source: Not attested to a date in the held record.

lost.source: Per the fed's own 19 February 1998 broadcast, recalling this title change.

won.source: Won by pinfall (Crash Landing) from the All Americans.
Not attested to a date in the held record.

lost.source: Lost by pinfall to the Freedom Fighters.

title: wwfl-cruiserweight
label: "Stone Cold" Mcdowd

won.source: Not attested to a date in the held record.

lost.source: The fed's own 27 April 1998 broadcast recalls this holder's earlier Cruiserweight Championship days before he became a WWFL headliner; no further detail on this reign's own dates or ending survives.

note: This holder is the same wrestler already on this wing's own held record as its former World Heavyweight Champion.

title: wwfl-cruiserweight
label: Inferno

won.source: Not attested to a date in the held record.

lost.source: Held as of the fed's own 11 March 1998 broadcast; a later champion is attested by 27 April 1998, with no further detail on this reign's own ending surviving.

note: Already champion by the fed's own 11 March 1998 broadcast, where he challenges the Trickster for the Intercontinental Championship alone; his own Cruiserweight belt is not contested in that match.

won.source: Already champion by the held record's first-served Cruiserweight Championship match, 27 April 1998.
Wins by pinfall (Doggpounder) at the fed's own Memorial Mayhem pay-per-view; the special guest referee, the WWFL president, is revealed to have been working with this holder throughout the match.

Already champion by the held record's first-served Television Championship defense, Spring Breakout '98, 27 April 1998; an earlier champion preceded this reign, not established to a servable standard in the held record.
